title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Disputes over Negotiable Instruments

articles.content_en: Where a dispute arises from the exercise of rights on an instrument or non-instrument rights under the Negotiable Instruments Law, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Where, in accordance with Article 10 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, an instrument debtor (i.e., the drawer) institutes an action on the grounds that the underlying relationship before the instrument was transferred is illegal, that the parties do not have a genuine transaction relationship or creditor-debt relationship, or that the holder should have paid consideration but failed to do so, requesting the return of the instrument, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Where, in accordance with Article 36 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, after the instrument has been dishonored by acceptance, dishonored by payment, or after the time limit for presentment for payment of a bill of exchange or check has been exceeded, the instrument holder endorses and transfers the instrument, and the endorsee institutes an action against the endorser as defendant to exercise the right of recourse, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Where a holder institutes an action after exercising the right of recourse first instead of first exercising the right to claim payment and is refused, the People's Court shall not accept the case. Except for the circumstances provided in Article 61, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Law and Article 3 of these Provisions, a holder may exercise the right of recourse only when, after first exercising the right to claim payment against the payer, payment is not obtained.

The right to claim payment is the first-priority right enjoyed by the holder; the right of recourse is the second-priority right enjoyed by the holder, namely, the right to request the endorser, the drawer, and other obligors of the bill of exchange to pay the amounts and expenses specified in Article 70, paragraph 1 of the Negotiable Instruments Law where, upon maturity of the bill of exchange, payment is refused, or circumstances specified in Article 61, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Law exist.

Actions instituted due to negotiable instrument disputes shall, according to law, be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the place of payment of the instrument or the domicile of the defendant.
The place of payment of an instrument refers to the place of payment specified on the instrument. Where no place of payment is specified on the instrument, the place of payment of the instrument shall be the business site, domicile, or habitual residence of the payer or agent payer of a bill of exchange, the business site of the drawer of a promissory note, or the business site of the payer or agent payer of a check. An agent payer is the authorized agent of the payer, referring to a financial institution such as a bank or credit cooperative that pays the amount of the instrument on behalf of the payer according to the payer's authorization.
II. Preservation of Negotiable Instruments

In a negotiable instrument action, the burden of adducing evidence shall be borne by the party who asserts a claim.
In accordance with Article 4, paragraph 2, Article 10, Article 12, and Article 21 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, a holder who institutes an action with the People's Court has the obligation to provide the instrument in dispute. Where the drawing, acceptance, delivery, or endorsement and transfer of the instrument is suspected of involving illegal acts such as fraud, theft, coercion, intimidation, or violence, the holder shall bear the burden of proving the legality of holding the instrument.

Where an instrument debtor raises a defense against a holder with whom it has a direct creditor-debt relationship in accordance with Article 13 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, and the People's Court consolidates the trial of the instrument relationship and the underlying relationship, the holder shall provide corresponding evidence proving that the agreed obligations have been performed.

Where the payer or acceptor is declared bankrupt by the People's Court according to law, a holder who institutes an action with the People's Court due to exercising the right of recourse shall provide the accepting court with the bankruptcy ruling made by the People's Court according to law or other evidence capable of proving the bankruptcy of the payer or acceptor.

In a negotiable instrument action, the party to the instrument bearing the burden of adducing evidence shall provide evidence before the conclusion of court debate in the first-instance People's Court. Where, due to objective reasons, evidence cannot be provided within the above-mentioned time limit for adducing evidence, an application for extension shall be made to the People's Court before the expiration of the time limit for adducing evidence. The extended period shall be determined by the People's Court based on the specific circumstances of the case.
Where a party to the instrument conceals the instrument or intentionally fails to provide evidence during the trial by the first-instance People's Court, it shall bear the corresponding litigation consequences.
IV. Rights on Instruments and Defenses

The rights of a holder against the drawer and acceptor of an instrument as provided in Article 17, paragraph 1, items (1) and (2) of the Negotiable Instruments Law include the right to claim payment and the right of recourse.

Where an instrument debtor raises a defense against the holder of an instrument that has already been endorsed and transferred on the grounds of Article 10 or Article 21 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, the People's Court shall not support the defense.

Where the drawer or endorser of an instrument is declared bankrupt, and the payer or acceptor pays or accepts without knowledge of such fact, the right of recourse arising therefrom may be registered as a bankruptcy claim, with the payer or acceptor as the creditor.

The right of recourse of a holder against prior parties as provided in Article 17, paragraph 1, items (3) and (4) of the Negotiable Instruments Law does not include the right of recourse against the drawer of the instrument.

The loss by a holder of the right of recourse against prior parties as provided in Article 40, paragraph 2 and Article 65 of the Negotiable Instruments Law does not include the right of recourse against the drawer of the instrument.

Where the limitation period for rights on an instrument as provided in Article 17 of the Negotiable Instruments Law is interrupted, the interruption shall be effective only as to the party in respect of whom the cause of interruption occurred.

Whether the written notice provided in Article 66, paragraph 1 of the Negotiable Instruments Law is overdue shall be determined by the date on which the holder or a prior party sends the written notice; where notice is given by letter, the date shown by the postmark of the letter shall prevail.

The interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China as referred to in Articles 70 and 71 of the Negotiable Instruments Law means the loan interest rate for enterprises' working capital for the same period as prescribed by the People's Bank of China.

Where an agent payer, after making payment in good faith in accordance with the prescribed procedures before the announcement of the public summons is published by the People's Court, the acceptor or payer refuses to reimburse the agent payer for the amount already advanced on the ground that the public summons has already been made, the People's Court shall not support such refusal.
V. Remedies for Loss of Instrument

After the loss of an instrument, where the person who lost the instrument directly applies to the People's Court for a public summons or institutes an action, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Where a check for which the drawer has authorized supplementary recording and has already affixed its signature is lost, and the person who lost the check applies to the People's Court for a public summons according to law, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

The person who lost an instrument who may apply for a public summons as provided in Article 15, paragraph 3 of the Negotiable Instruments Law refers to the last lawful holder of an instrument that may be endorsed and transferred according to the regulations before such person lost possession of the instrument.

Where a bank bill of exchange for which the drawer has affixed its signature but the agent payer has not been recorded is lost, and the person who lost the bill applies to the People's Court of the place where the payer, i.e., the issuing bank, is located for a public summons according to law, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

After the loss of an instrument for which the time limit for presentment for payment has been exceeded, where the person who lost the instrument applies for a public summons, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Where the People's Court decides to accept an application for a public summons, it shall simultaneously notify the payer and the agent payer to stop payment, and shall issue an announcement within three days from the date of case filing.

Upon receipt of the notice to stop payment issued by the People's Court, the payer or agent payer shall immediately stop payment until the conclusion of the procedure of public summons. Where payment is released without the permission of the People's Court that issued the notice to stop payment, the liability on the instrument shall not be exempted.

The announcement shall be published in a national newspaper or other media, and on the same day be posted in the announcement column of the People's Court. If there is a stock exchange at the place where the People's Court is located, the announcement shall also be published on the same day at that stock exchange.

In accordance with Article 219 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), the period of the announcement shall not be less than sixty days, and the expiration date of the period of the public summons shall not be earlier than fifteen days after the date of payment of the instrument.

In accordance with Article 220, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law, during the period of the public summons, where a negotiable instrument subject to the public summons is pledged or discounted, and the holder who accepts the instrument as a result of the pledge or discount claims rights on the instrument, the People's Court shall not support the claim, except where the instrument was acquired after the expiration of the period of the public summons but before the People's Court renders a judgment on the invalidation of the instrument.

After the loss of an instrument, where the person who lost the instrument, before the expiration of the limitation period for rights on the instrument, requests the drawer to reissue the instrument or requests the debtor to pay, and institutes an action due to the debtor's refusal to pay or the drawer's refusal to reissue the instrument while providing corresponding security, the action shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the domicile of the defendant or the place of payment of the instrument.

Where the person who lost an instrument institutes an action with the People's Court because the drawer refuses to reissue the instrument or the debtor refuses to pay, the defendant shall be the drawer who has an instrument creditor-debt relationship with the person who lost the instrument, or the payer or acceptor of the instrument who refuses to pay.

Where the person who lost an instrument, in order to exercise ownership of the instrument, requests the unlawful holder of the instrument to return the instrument, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Where the person who lost an instrument institutes an action with the People's Court, the person shall explain to the People's Court the circumstances of having previously held the instrument and losing the instrument. The People's Court shall, based on the specific circumstances of the case, decide whether the party shall provide security and the amount of the security.

With respect to a party who falsely reports the loss of an instrument, after verifying the facts and ruling to terminate the procedure of public summons or the litigation procedure, the People's Court may, by reference to Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law, pursue the legal liability of the person making the false report.
VI. Validity of Negotiable Instruments

In accordance with Article 108 of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Measures for the Implementation of the Administration of Negotiable Instruments approved by the State Council, where a party to an instrument uses an instrument that is not in the uniform format prescribed by the People's Bank of China, the matter shall be determined in accordance with the Measures for the Implementation of the Administration of Negotiable Instruments, except for instruments issued outside the territory of China.

Where the drawer of a bank bill of exchange or a bank promissory note or the acceptor of a bank acceptance bill does not affix the prescribed special seal on the instrument but affixes the official seal of the bank, or the drawer of a check does not affix the financial seal consistent with the seal reserved by the unit at the bank but affixes the official seal of the drawer, the person affixing the signature or seal shall bear liability on the instrument.

In accordance with Article 9 of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Measures for the Implementation of the Administration of Negotiable Instruments, where the amount in Chinese capital characters on an instrument is inconsistent with the amount in figures, or the amount recorded on the instrument, the date of issue or the date of drawing, or the name of the payee is altered, or a seal of a banking department is affixed in place of a special seal in violation of regulations, and the payer or agent payer makes payment on such an instrument, the payer or agent payer shall bear liability.

Where an action is instituted due to a dispute arising from the alteration of the actual settlement amount of a bank bill of exchange and a party requests confirmation of the validity of the bill, the People's Court shall determine that the bank bill of exchange is invalid.

Where a holder of a blank authorized instrument, when exercising rights on the instrument, fails to fully complete the necessary particulars to be recorded on the instrument, and institutes an action because the payer or agent payer refuses to accept the instrument, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Where the signature or seal of the endorser, acceptor, or guarantor of an instrument on the instrument does not conform to the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Measures for the Implementation of the Administration of Negotiable Instruments, or where a person without capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct affixes a signature or seal on the instrument, such signature or seal shall be invalid, but this shall not affect the People's Court's determination of the validity of other signatures or seals on the instrument.
VII. Endorsement of Negotiable Instruments

Where an action is instituted due to a dispute arising from a pledgee of an instrument re-endorsing the pledged instrument for pledge or for transfer by endorsement, the People's Court shall determine that the act of endorsement is invalid.

In accordance with Article 27 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where the drawer of an instrument records the phrase "non-negotiable" on the instrument and the instrument holder endorses and transfers the instrument, the act of endorsement is invalid. The transferee after the endorsement and transfer shall not enjoy rights on the instrument, and the drawer and acceptor of the instrument shall not bear liability on the instrument to the transferee.

In accordance with Articles 27 and 30 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where an endorser delivers the instrument to another person without recording the name of the endorsee, the recording by the holder of its own name in the column for the endorsee on the instrument shall have the same legal effect as a recording made by the endorser.

In accordance with Article 31 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, the first endorser in a chain of consecutive endorsements shall be the payee recorded on the instrument, and the last holder of the instrument shall be the endorsee of the last endorsement.

In accordance with Articles 34 and 35 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where an endorser records on the instrument the phrases "non-negotiable", "entrusted for collection", or "pledge", and a subsequent party re-endorses the instrument for transfer, entrusted collection, or pledge, the original endorser shall not bear liability on the instrument to the endorsee of the subsequent party, but this shall not affect the liability on the instrument of the drawer, the acceptor, or the prior parties of the original endorser.

In accordance with Article 57, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where a lender engages in pledge loan business on instruments with malicious intent or gross negligence, the People's Court shall determine that the act of pledge is invalid.

In accordance with Article 27 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where the drawer records the phrase "non-negotiable" on the instrument and a subsequent party discounts or pledges the instrument, and a holder who acquired the instrument through such discount or pledge claims rights on the instrument, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

In accordance with Articles 34 and 35 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where an endorser records the phrase "non-negotiable" on the instrument and a subsequent party discounts or pledges the instrument, the original endorser shall not bear liability on the instrument to the endorsee of the subsequent party.

In accordance with Article 35, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where a bill of exchange is pledged, if the pledgor only records the phrase "pledge" on the bill without affixing a signature or seal on the instrument, or if the pledgor does not record the phrase "pledge" on the bill or an allonge but separately concludes a pledge contract or pledge clauses, such act does not constitute a pledge of the negotiable instrument.

Where a holder of a commercial bill of exchange applies for discounting from a bank with which it does not maintain an account, such application shall have the same legal effect as an application for discounting from the bank with which it has opened a deposit account, except where the holder acts with malicious intent or colludes maliciously with the discounting bank.

Issuing a bill of exchange in violation of the prescribed region, endorsing and transferring a bank bill of exchange, or issuing, endorsing and transferring bank promissory notes or checks across the bill exchange area in violation of the provisions on administration of negotiable instruments shall not affect the liability on the instrument that the drawer or endorser shall bear according to law.

In accordance with Article 36 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, where the instrument is dishonored by acceptance, dishonored by payment, or the time limit for presentment for payment has been exceeded, and the instrument holder endorses and transfers the instrument, the endorser shall bear liability on the instrument.

Where an acceptor or payer pays a holder who presents the instrument for payment after the prescribed time limit in accordance with Article 53, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Law, such payment shall have the same legal effect as payment made within the prescribed time limit.
VIII. Guarantee of Negotiable Instruments

Where a state organ, a public institution established for public welfare purposes, or a social organization acts as a guarantor of a negotiable instrument, the guarantee of the negotiable instrument is invalid, except where a state organ provides the guarantee of the negotiable instrument for the purpose of onlending loans from foreign governments or international economic organizations as approved by the State Council.
Where a guarantee of a negotiable instrument is invalid, the guarantor of the instrument shall bear civil liability corresponding to its fault.

Where a guarantor does not record the phrase "guarantee" on the instrument or allonge but separately concludes a guarantee contract or guarantee clauses, it does not constitute a guarantee of a negotiable instrument, and the People's Court shall apply the relevant provisions of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China.
IX. Application of Law

When the People's Court tries a case involving a dispute over a negotiable instrument, the provisions of the Negotiable Instruments Law shall apply; where the Negotiable Instruments Law has no provisions, laws such as the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China and administrative regulations formulated by the State Council shall apply.
Where the relevant administrative rules formulated and published by the People's Bank of China do not conflict with laws and administrative regulations, they may be applied by reference.

Where a party to an instrument institutes an action because it is dissatisfied with a specific administrative act of the financial administrative department, the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, the Negotiable Instruments Law, and the Measures for the Implementation of the Administration of Negotiable Instruments and other provisions on the administration of negotiable instruments shall apply.
Where the relevant administrative rules formulated and published by the People's Bank of China do not conflict with laws and administrative regulations, they may be applied by reference.

Where the People's Court retries a case involving a dispute over a negotiable instrument for which a final judgment has already been rendered before the Negotiable Instruments Law came into force, the Negotiable Instruments Law shall not apply.
X. Legal Liability

Article 66: In accordance with the provisions of Article 14, Article 102 and Article 103 of the Law on Negotiable Instruments, a person who forges or alters an instrument shall, in addition to bearing criminal and administrative liability according to law, also bear civil liability for compensation if losses are caused to others. A person whose signature or seal is forged shall not bear instrument liability.

Article 67: Where supplementary recording is made to matters not recorded or not fully recorded on an instrument, and the supplementary matters exceed the scope of authorization, the drawer shall bear instrument liability for the supplemented instrument. If losses are caused to others, the drawer shall also bear corresponding civil liability.

Article 68: If a payer or an agent payer fails to identify a forged or altered instrument or identity document and makes erroneous payment, this constitutes "gross negligence" as provided in Article 57 of the Law on Negotiable Instruments, and if losses are caused to the holder, it shall bear civil liability according to law. After bearing liability, the payer or agent payer shall have the right to seek recourse from the forger or alterer according to law.
If the holder is at fault, it shall also bear corresponding civil liability.
Article 71: Where a party causes losses to others due to an erroneous application for preservation of an instrument, it shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 72: Where losses are caused to others because the drawer issued a check drawn on insufficient funds or a check whose signature style or seal does not match the drawer's reserved signature or seal, the drawer and the endorser of the check shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 73: When a People's Court, in hearing a case of instrument dispute, discovers clues of a suspected crime of instrument fraud that are connected with the case but do not fall under the same legal relationship, it shall promptly provide the clues of criminal suspicion to the relevant public security organ; however, the trial of the instrument dispute case shall not be suspended for this reason.

Article 74: In accordance with the provisions of Article 104 of the Law on Negotiable Instruments, where losses are caused to a party because a staff member of a financial institution neglects his duty in instrument business and accepts, pays, discounts or guarantees an instrument that violates the provisions of the Law on Negotiable Instruments, the financial institution and the directly responsible person shall bear joint and several liability according to law.

Article 75: In accordance with the provisions of Article 106 of the Law on Negotiable Instruments, where losses are caused to others because the drawer made the instrument, or other instrument debtors signed or sealed on the instrument not in accordance with statutory conditions, they shall, in addition to bearing instrument liability according to the matters recorded, also bear corresponding civil liability.
Where the holder accepts the instrument with knowledge or constructive knowledge of the circumstances in the preceding paragraph, the liability of the drawer or the instrument debtor may be appropriately mitigated.
